title: Witten: Townsend Brown's antigravity bismuth isotope

tellings.quote: he says that he was contracted by right Airfield to work on gravity and he said that there was a guy named townzen who had a weird isotope of bismuth that exhibited anti-gravity properties

plain: In the 1950s, the physicist Louis Witten says, Wright Field, an Air Force base in Ohio, hired him to work on gravity, and he heard of a man called Townsend who had a strange form of the metal bismuth that seemed to resist gravity. Michels passes this on from what Witten said, and connects the man to Thomas Townsend Brown, an inventor known for propulsion experiments; the story is tied to the Martin Corporation, an aircraft maker. If it is true, the military was seriously chasing anti-gravity materials in the 1950s.
